title: Lakestone pilot weekly: compliance tuning & SSO review
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on SSO integration progress, audit log format, data retention policy alignment, and preliminary SOC 2 evidence checklist. Agreed on two benchmark runs for latency/cost after SSO enforced; next security artifacts to be uploaded to shared folder.
next_steps: Redwood to push SAML metadata for test IdP by 2026-12-20
Lakestone to validate SSO sign-on and report failures by 2026-12-22
Redwood to run two benchmark suites with SSO enforced and share heatmap by 2026-12-23
Exchange SOC 2 evidence mapping spreadsheet by 2026-12-24
action_items: Priya Malhotra: provide SAML testing instructions and debug checklist; due 2026-12-20
Maya Chen: provide example audit log samples for compliance team; due 2026-12-22
Connor Lee: set up logging retention policy demo in staging (7/30/365 buckets); due 2026-12-21
Evan Ross: confirm internal stakeholder for SOC 2 evidence review; due 2026-12-24
header:
Date: 2026-12-17 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 mins | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jamie Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Connor Lee (Redwood SRE); Evan Ross (Lakestone CTO), Maya Chen (Lakestone Infosec), Ravi Patel (Lakestone Data Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Lakestone PM)
transcript:
00:00 Jamie Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll get started in a minute, uh, couple people joining late i see
00:14 Evan Ross: yeah just hopped in, sorry about that, flight delay this morning
00:18 Jamie Ortiz: all good, quick agenda — SSO check, audit logs, retention mapping, SOC2 artifacts, then tuning and benchmarks, any additions?
00:30 Maya Chen: i wanna make sure we block time to review the log fields; we need user identifiers and request ids for our SIEM
00:39 Priya Malhotra: absolutely, we've captured request_id, session_id and subject/username but the mapping to your internal user_id might need a transform step
00:50 Ravi Patel: can you clarify transform step? we try to avoid PII in logs so want to hash or pseudonymize
01:01 Priya Malhotra: yep that's expected — we can provide a pipeline example that hashes email to a stable id before sending to your log collector, will note that in the doc
01:15 Jamie Ortiz: quick SSO status, priya — you pushed the SAML metadata into the staging tenant yesterday?
01:22 Priya Malhotra: yes, uploaded metadata and created an SP entry, but we saw a mismatch on NameID format with Lakestone IdP; i'm 95% sure it's an attribute mapping setting on their end
01:35 Maya Chen: we use transient NameID by default, but we can switch to persistent if required, does Redwood require persistent?
01:42 Priya Malhotra: we can work with both, persistent simplifies session correlation across services but it's not a hard requirement; we can also pass an email attribute as NameID
01:55 Maya Chen: ok we'll try persistent for the test
02:05 Jamie Ortiz: good. On audit logs — conner, can you walk through retention buckets and where audit streams land?
02:12 Connor Lee: sure, in the pilot staging we route audit logs to a dedicated audit cluster in our region, default retention is 90 days, we also support tiering to 30/180/365 depending on the contract; logs are immutable append-only once ingested
02:29 Evan Ross: immutable is important for us — can we get a WORM style retention for 90 days?
02:36 Connor Lee: yes, we can enable WORM for the audit bucket, it just prevents deletion until retention window expires, we'll show a quick demo in staging
02:48 Ravi Patel: does WORM also prevent redact requests? we have to support subject delete under GDPR
02:55 Connor Lee: great question. WORM prevents deletions at storage layer but our data retention flow allows redaction by replacing PII fields in the index and marking records as redacted; raw storage still holds the original until retention end unless you request a permanent purge via legal/contract path
03:17 Maya Chen: so there is an extra step for purge, we need that spelled out for legal — please include the purge process and timelines in the artifact set
03:28 Jamie Ortiz: noted, we'll add purge process and the legal reqs. SOC 2 — evan, what's your expected timeline for evidence review?
03:38 Evan Ross: our compliance team wants to have initial artifacts by Jan 5, 2027 and a draft mapping to their control IDs by Jan 12, 2027
03:47 Jamie Ortiz: ok we can commit to that, priya will assemble the evidence pack — items like config screenshots, SSO SAML metadata, log retention settings, access control lists, RBAC configs
03:58 Priya Malhotra: small note, some screenshots show different UI labels in staging vs prod, i'll annotate them in the doc to avoid confusion
04:08 Sofia Alvarez: on the pilot results — we ran the baseline run with 1k concurrent requests, average p50 p90 latency numbers were shared last week but we need them with SSO turned on
04:22 Priya Malhotra: enabling SAML adds an auth roundtrip, but once session cookie is minted the per-token latency is same; we'll run bench with SSO enforced to capture worst-case cold sign-on overhead
04:36 Ravi Patel: for cost modeling, can you emit token counts separately? our finance team needs per-call token + infra cost estimates
04:45 Jamie Ortiz: yes, we'll include token accounting and an infra delta for auth overhead, estimate should be <5% on steady state but cold sign-ons may spike CPU briefly
04:58 Maya Chen: about audit fields — important fields for us: timestamp, request_id, model_name, user_id (pseudonymized), action, token_count, cost, response_hash — can you confirm response_hash is included?
05:18 Priya Malhotra: we currently compute a response_hash (sha256) for response dedupe and quality checks; we can include that in the audit stream
05:28 Evan Ross: and can you show an example line of the audit event we can drop straight into our SIEM?
05:34 Priya Malhotra: yes i'll paste sample in shared sheet after this call
05:38 Jamie Ortiz: one of the compliance folks asked about key management — are you using KMS? is customer-managed KMS supported in Private mode?
05:46 Connor Lee: on Hosted we use an HSM-backed KMS and we support customer-managed keys for Private deployments via KMS integrations, for Dedicated we offer bring-your-own-KMS option as well
05:59 Maya Chen: we need EKM/HSM proof and certs for the hosted endpoint, can you share attestation or whitepaper?
06:07 Jamie Ortiz: we'll upload the KMS whitepaper and HSM attestation to the shared security folder, priya will link it in the SOC2 mapping sheet
06:17 Ravi Patel: small snag — when we enabled SSO in staging earlier we saw about 3% of requests log as anonymous; not sure why
06:24 Priya Malhotra: that typically occurs when a bearer session expires mid-call and the call falls back to service-account token; we'll instrument and surface counts per minute so you can spot spikes
06:36 Maya Chen: please add a metric in dashboard for anonymous request ratio and a heartbeat alert at 0.5% threshold, that should trigger ops review
06:46 Connor Lee: we can add that to the console, settable alert, we'll add as an example rule in the runbook
06:55 Jamie Ortiz: status on SAML mismatch — may a quick check, evan can you share your IdP metadata after the call?
07:02 Evan Ross: yes, i'll put metadata in the shared folder by EOD, also will share logs showing the NameID error
07:09 Priya Malhotra: great, once we have that i'll reconfigure mapping rules in staging and run sign-on tests with persistent NameID
07:18 Sofia Alvarez: can you walk through how audit logs link back to user actions in our product? we need to map product request ids to model calls
07:28 Priya Malhotra: we can accept an optional x-correlation-id header from your front end that we pass through to the runtime and it appears on all audit events; that will be the join key you want
07:41 Ravi Patel: perfect. we'll start instrumenting x-correlation-id in our dev builds tomorrow
07:47 Jamie Ortiz: SOC 2 evidence pack — list of artifacts we'll provide: SSO configuration, IdP-SP metadata exchange, RBAC snapshot, audit log samples, retention policy docs, incident response runbook extract, KMS attestation
08:05 Maya Chen: for RBAC snapshot, include a list of roles and their privileges, we need to validate least privilege
08:14 Priya Malhotra: we'll export role maps from staging and highlight differences versus prod labels
08:21 Evan Ross: on data residency — are logs stored in eu-west-1 for our EU customers? we have users in eire and need the logs to stay in region
08:31 Connor Lee: yes, you can choose region for audit cluster; for this pilot we've provisioned eu-west-1 and us-west-2 as requested in the initial ticket
08:40 Maya Chen: retention deletion flow question — if a user requests delete, will the corresponding audit event be redacted and how long will that action take?
08:49 Connor Lee: redaction pipeline runs in batch within 24 hours of request; final purge is a separate legal workflow and may take up to 30 days after legal approval depending on contract
08:58 Sofia Alvarez: okay please list the exact SLAs for redaction and purge in the artifact set
09:07 Jamie Ortiz: agreed. any blockers preventing Jan 5 artifact delivery?
09:15 Evan Ross: none from our side, only dependency is your updated SSO test metadata and the log sample template
09:22 Jamie Ortiz: we'll get that over — priya will follow up with the metadata and conner will deliver the log retention demo snapshot
09:30 Priya Malhotra: i'll schedule a 30 minute SAML debug session if the IdP metadata doesn't resolve the mismatch
09:39 Maya Chen: thanks, that would help. also is there any additional cost to enable WORM? we need cost delta
09:46 Connor Lee: small monthly premium for WORM storage, i'll include a cost delta per GB in the benchmark spreadsheet
09:55 Ravi Patel: regarding token accounting, can you provide a CSV with token counts per model call for our baseline traces?
10:03 Priya Malhotra: yes we'll provide per-call token CSVs, include input tokens, output tokens, model name, and timestamp, that'll feed your finance model
10:13 Jamie Ortiz: ok let's summarize next steps then — SAML metadata, audit samples, redaction SLA, WORM cost delta, benchmark runs with SSO enforced, SOC2 artifact spreadsheet — owners align with action items above
10:32 Evan Ross: sounds good, we'll validate sign-on and run first internal acceptance tests by Dec 22
10:40 Jamie Ortiz: perfect, thanks everyone, we'll recap in an email and post artifacts into the shared security folder, see you next week
10:48 Meeting ended
notes: Shared folder: https://redwood-sharing.example.com/s/lakestone-poc-security | Benchmarks sheet: /sheets/lakestone-benchmarks | SOC2 mapping: /docs/lakestone-soc2-mapping.xlsx
